newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao arrives at heavily-guarded court.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao arrives at heavily-guarded court.

text.p: Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao arrived at a heavily-guarded makeshift court on Wednesday to face criminal forgery charges.
Paramilitary commandos ushered the 75-year-old leader from a bullet-proof car to an annexe at New Delhi's Vigyan Bhavan conference hall complex for his first appearance in the 1989 case.

In the courtroom, Rao was flanked by two plainclothes paramilitary commandos and given a front seat away from three other people accused in the case, including a former minister and a religious Hindu guru close to the ex-prime minister.
Rao sat expressionless in a court that had allowed only 12 reporters and a few members of his Congress party to be present for the hearing.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's federal police, on September 26 charged Rao and the three others with involvement in an alleged attempt in 1989 to defame V.P. Singh, an opposition leader who later became prime minister.
They are alleged to have forged documents which aimed to show that Singh's son held $21 million in a bank account on the Caribbean island of St Kitts. Rao has not commented publicly on the case.
